lens: Single bounded pre-implementation follow-up on accepted 810-D1: invocation/citation scope, classification groups, and composed delivered-bundle acceptance

counterweight_triage.concern: 810-D1: complete citation equality versus classification-group membership
counterweight_triage.disposition: The repaired contract distinguishes invocation, citation, and classification scopes. Each complete citation must be a nonempty subset of the invocation and must exactly equal packet and observation targets, without intersection with a classification group. Duplicate/cardinality checks remain mandatory. Each group's coverage and applicable floors use its own issue numbers.

counterweight_triage.concern: Validated evidence transfer could bypass verification
counterweight_triage.disposition: The grouped owner retains invocation context, validates each cited delivered bundle once, and passes only that call-local validated result to covered groups. Existing binding joins remain mandatory, verified packet bytes are returned without rereading, and caller injection of unvalidated cached approval is explicitly forbidden.

counterweight_triage.concern: Separate happy paths could conceal the original composition failure
counterweight_triage.disposition: Acceptance now explicitly requires one mixed bug/feature fixture using one delivered two-target packet and one citation through draft, hook, staged, pre-push, plural CLI, and pause-to-close dispatch. Both group reports must succeed; removing either applicable floor must fail. Critique-exempt classifications retain their exemption.

next_move: Implement the repaired 810-D1 contract and its composed acceptance fixture; no remaining D1 design flaw was identified.
non_claims: Reviewed all four supplied inline semantic payloads. The supplied code establishes the existing scope coupling; this verdict assesses whether the repair contract is implementable.
No workspace edits, tests, provider operations, nested delegation, or additional review round.
This is bounded design disposition only, not implementation verification, behavioral proof, release approval, or Goal #805 / issue #810 resolution approval.
